The Department’s scholars recognize that these challenges are overlapping and interconnected in ways that demand coordinated and integrated evidence-based solutions that utilize big data and state-of-the-art analytic methods to identify novel risk factors and associated precision public health and policy approaches to improve human health. To do so, the DPPHS conducts research that leverages its location in one of the largest and most diverse populations in the urban United States—Los Angeles County—as well as its collaborations with partners across the United States and globally. We seek an accomplished scientist with a PhD or equivalent degree in Public Health, Social and Behavioral Sciences, or a related discipline, whose research program focuses on digital environments and their influence on health behavior. The successful candidate will have expertise in computational social science and the study of social media and digital platform ecosystems, including platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, and/or emerging digital environments, and will examine how these platforms shape health behaviors through mechanisms such as influencer marketing, digital advertising, and other commercial determinants of health, incorporating theoretical principles of health communication. Particular emphasis will be placed on research that investigates tobacco, nicotine, cannabis, or related substance use products, especially in relation to youth and young adult populations.The ideal candidate will also have experience evaluating the behavioral and perceptual impact of digital health content, including the use of experimental or quasi-experimental designs to assess how exposure to online messaging influences attitudes, risk perceptions, and health behaviors. jobs.description: Public Relations Public Relations Home Campus Calendars Campus Connection Frequently Used Forms Press Releases Siskiyous Style Guide (contact Public Relations) Staff Web Content Year-End Reviews Foundation Eagle's Nest Resale Shop Foundation College of the Siskiyous Paramedic Program Instructor Theresa Gowan Honored with Statewide Clinical Excellence Award For Immediate Release: May 21, 2026 Public Relations Office Dawnie Slabaugh Phone: (530) 938-5373 Email: slabaugh@siskiyous.edu Weed / COS – College of the Siskiyous is proud to announce that Theresa Gowan, Lead Faculty of the College of the Siskiyous / Mendocino College Satellite Paramedic Program Training Center has been selected as a recipient of the prestigious Clinical Excellence Award from the California Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Authority as part of this year's statewide EMS Awards program Selected from a highly competitive pool of more than 175 nominations submitted from across California, this recognition highlights Gowan's exceptional clinical skill, dedication, and unwavering commitment to patient care in the emergency medical services profession. "The dedication and commitment demonstrated through this nomination exemplify the highest standards of clinical care in the EMS profession," said Ashley Williams, Deputy Director of Legislative and External Affairs in an email announcement. "We are honored to recognize individuals whose work reflects such excellence and impact in patient care." The Clinical Excellence Award recognizes EMS professionals who consistently demonstrate superior clinical performance, critical thinking, and compassionate care in high-pressure environments. Theresa Gowan's selection reflects not only individual achievement but also the strength and professionalism of the broader EMS community. Gowan was formally notified of the award in March, with an official award presentation by Kirk Thomsen – Paramedic Program Director & EMS Coordinator and Dr. Jeremiah Sims – Dean of Career & Technical Education on April 3. "We are incredibly proud of Theresa Gowan for receiving this well-deserved statewide recognition. Her selection from such a competitive field of nominees across California is a testament to the high caliber of instruction and clinical expertise she brings to our Paramedic Program," said Dr. Char Perlas, Superintendent/President. "At College of the Siskiyous, we strive for excellence in our Career and Technical Education programs, and Theresa embodies the dedication, skill, and compassion we hope to instill in all our students. This award not only honors her individual mastery of the profession but also highlights the strength of the partnership between Siskiyous and Mendocino College in preparing the next generation of EMS first responders." About the EMS Awards Program The California EMS Awards program recognizes outstanding individuals and organizations that exemplify excellence, leadership, and innovation in emergency medical services. Honorees are selected based on their impact, professionalism, and dedication to advancing quality patient care throughout the state. About the College of the Siskiyous EMS/Paramedic Program The Paramedic Program trains students to provide immediate care to the critically ill and injured. Paramedics determine the nature and extent of illness or injury, provide advanced life support, communicate with emergency medical services personnel and transport patients to the hospital. The paramedic program is a highly interactive, fast paced, hands-on experience, requiring student participation. This program meets or exceeds all state and national guidelines for paramedic training, and includes Anatomy and Physiology, Advanced Cardiac Life Support, Pediatric Advanced Life Support, Pediatric Education for Pre-hospital Providers, Advanced Medical Life Support, International Trauma Life Support, and Geriatric Emergency Medical Services. Students who successfully complete the requirements for this program will be prepared for the Paramedic National Registry examination. The curriculum may also academically prepare the student to transfer to a four-year university to complete a Baccalaureate degree program. Learn more about the Paramedic program at College of the Siskiyous or send an email to cteinfo@siskiyous.edu.

The program emphasizes our strengths in biomedical research and is supplemented by technologies developed here and elsewhere to accelerate breakthroughs in both thought and practice. The great 16th century astronomer, engineer, physicist and polymath Galileo Galilei once said: “You cannot teach a person anything; you can only help them find it within.” At Sanford Burnham Prebys, Galileo’s words reflect the didactic, tutorial and laboratory-based emphases of our graduate program, which is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in biomedical sciences while engaging in projects with our biological, chemistry, bioinformatics and engineering faculty and a specialized focus on main areas studied within a laboratory. San Diego is renowned for both its scientific excellence and recreational opportunities. As a national and international hub for life sciences research, the region is home to numerous academic institutions and industry leaders. With a moderate year-round climate, pristine beaches to the west, and mountains and desert to the east, it’s an ideal place to live and learn. I encourage you to explore these pages to discover why pursuing science and graduate education at Sanford Burnham Prebys could be the right choice for you.
